note: Let k=(a^2+b^2)/(ab+1). For a hypothetical nonsquare k choose a+b minimal and assume a>=b. Since k>=2, f(b)=(2-k)b^2-k<0 for f(x)=x^2-kbx+b^2-k, so a is the larger root and a'=kb-a<b. If a'<0, set c=-a'>0; Vieta gives a-c=kb and k=b^2+ac, hence a(1-bc)=b^3+c>0, impossible. Thus a'>=0; a'=0 forces k=b^2 square, so a'>0 and (a',b) is a smaller positive solution with the same nonsquare k.
